findings.reason: The protected implementation is already clear, conventional randomized-geometry code. Its deterministic random adapter is compact, distance and angle name the two polar components directly, the square-root radial transform is visible, and the final list comprehension performs exactly the requested draws without unnecessary abstraction or naming defects, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode design problem 478 and its Python constructor plus randPoint interface. The app-local solve(radius, x_center, y_center, random_values, draws) adapter exposes the same geometry, consumes deterministic radial/angle pairs cyclically, returns the requested finite trace, and preserves the native requirement that every point lie inside or on the circle with an area-uniform distribution.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2064991373 use the same square-root radial transform, 2*pi angle transform, center translation, and coordinate construction. The reviewed difference is unavoidable judge plumbing: LeetCode stores constructor fields and draws from its hidden random source per randPoint call, while the offline app receives a deterministic stream and finite draw count. The alignment review is hash-bound to the revised Approach.

The legal 64-draw, 256-draw, and larger center-point workloads span at least 4x and isolate result construction as the declared size grows. The exact current source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.07x the calibrated reference runtime. A correct quadratic diagnostic that explicitly rebuilt the accumulated point list every eighth draw passed every opaque output but failed only performance at 12.92x the reference runtime.

Each app point consumes two stream values and performs constant arithmetic and trigonometric work, so draws points require O(draws) time and O(draws) returned storage. The native randPoint method produces one two-coordinate list with O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary state per call.

The current-targeted Approach exactly maps a uniform v to angle 2*pi*v, derives radius R*sqrt(u) from the disk area fraction, translates polar coordinates by the center, and explains the deterministic app stream. Its alternatives distinguish correct rejection sampling from the biased uniform-radius error, and the corrupted pi notation has been repaired to mathematical LaTeX.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the uniform-inside-circle objective, circumference inclusion, Solution constructor and randPoint return shape, the single operation/argument example with all three displayed random outputs and calls, all three constraints, and the absence of visuals, tables, follow-ups, or later sections; app-only deterministic fields are confined to the executable-contract explanation.
